subject: Urgent: load imbalance triage, temporary fallbacks, and roadmap decisions
messages:
From: Olivia Chen <olivia@fastcart.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Cc: ops@fastcart.com
Date: 2028-09-17 09:12 PDT
Subject: Abnormal latency/throughput — starting 08:50 PDT

Hi Neha,

We started seeing elevated tail latency and some timeouts on our checkout GenAPI calls starting ~08:50 PDT. Our engineers see request spikes to the gen route and a subset of requests returning 500 or timing out after 10s. This is impacting checkout flows for ~7% of sessions.

Can Redwood confirm whether there are any regional capacity problems or active rollouts that could explain this? We need a quick mitigation plan and a customer-facing note for our ops teams and product.

Thanks,
Olivia
VP Product, FastCart

From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>, Olivia Chen <olivia@fastcart.com>
Date: 2028-09-17 09:25 PDT
Subject: Re: Abnormal latency/throughput — starting 08:50 PDT

Ben/Karthik/Marissa — tagging you for immediate triage. Customer is seeing p99s spike and ~7% session failures on gen route. Key asks:
- Can SRE confirm whether any autoscale events, kernel rollouts, or model variant rollouts happened in us-west-2 between 08:30–09:10?
- If this is capacity/queueing, can we enact a temporary traffic steering rule to shift FastCart traffic to the fallback model variant?
- Product/Marissa: we need clarity on whether the KV-cache eviction mitigations we discussed (roadmap INF-3421) could have any short-term perf regressions if enabled. If that fix is not GA, we need explicit guidance.

I'm drafting a short customer note once we have the root cause hypothesis. Attaching initial logs we pulled.

Attachments: load_snapshot-20280917.json

Neha Kapoor
Senior Account Lead, Redwood Inference

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>, Olivia Chen <olivia@fastcart.com>
Date: 2028-09-17 10:02 PDT
Subject: Re: Abnormal latency/throughput — starting 08:50 PDT

Neha/Team — quick summary from initial triage (SRE):
- At ~08:45 we saw a concentrated burst of long-context requests from a FastCart tenant shard that caused KV cache churn on a subset of pods. That increased per-token compute and delayed kv-cache lookups, leading to backlog and p99 tail increases.
- No infra kernel or model rollout recorded in us-west-2 during the window. Autoscaler did open additional instances, but scale lag was ~60–90s during the peak which aggravated queues.
- We've enabled a transient limit on max-concurrent long-context requests for that shard and are routing new requests to a warm fallback variant (quantized) which reduces compute by ~30% per token.

Action items I recommend now:
1) Formalize the temporary fallback policy we just applied and get Product sign-off for up to 3 hours while we stabilize. See attached proposed_fallback_policy.md.
2) Product to confirm whether the KV-cache eviction work (INF-3421) is safe to ship as a targeted mitigation; if not, can we prioritize a backport/patch?
3) Ops: FastCart wants a short buyer-facing note with an ETA for a full mitigation and whether there are request-level workarounds (smaller max tokens, disable certain server-side context stitching).

I'll keep the temporary steering in place and monitor. Uploading an excerpt from the SRE playbook for the customer's timeline.

Attachments: proposed_fallback_policy.md, sre_playbook_excerpt.pdf

Ben Carter
SRE Manager, Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>, Olivia Chen <olivia@fastcart.com>
Date: 2028-09-17 11:05 PDT
Subject: Re: Abnormal latency/throughput — starting 08:50 PDT

Thanks for the triage Ben. A few product-side notes and asks:
- INF-3421 (KV cache eviction improvement) is currently scheduled for Q4 minor release; we do not have a safe backport in the current tree. We can evaluate an expedited patch but need eng capacity (risk: introduces subtle race on cache TTLs).
- Short-term: approve the fallback steering for up to 3 hours. We should also offer FastCart guidance to reduce client-side max_context_length for the next 24h — this will reduce cache churn.
- Mid-term: we need to prioritize adding a per-tenant long-request guardrail (configurable by account) to avoid a single shard causing node-level kv churn. I'll raise an RFC to the roadmap board; can someone from SRE provide an estimated dev/qa effort?

Proposed customer note (draft):
Hi Olivia — we observed a concentrated burst of long-context requests causing KV cache pressure on a subset of nodes. We’ve applied a short-lived fallback to a lower-CPU variant and added temporary concurrency limits. We recommend reducing max_context_length in the short term. Our teams are working on a permanent fix and will follow up with an ETA.

Neha — you can send this after Ben confirms attach window + monitoring thresholds.

Marissa Cole
Product Manager, Redwood Inference

From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Olivia Chen <olivia@fastcart.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-09-17 15:40 PDT
Subject: Re: Abnormal latency/throughput — starting 08:50 PDT

Olivia — quick customer-facing update below (short and actionable) — please let me know if you want different wording before I send on the official channel.

—Customer-facing note draft—
Hi Olivia and FastCart ops team,

Summary: At ~08:45 PDT we detected a concentrated burst of long-context generation requests that caused KV cache pressure on a subset of inference pods, which in turn drove tail latency and ~7% session failures.
What we did:
- Applied a temporary routing policy to move new requests to a lower-CPU fallback model variant.
- Imposed a short concurrency limit on long-context requests for the affected tenant shard.
- Monitoring is in place; we will revert the fallback once p99 latency is within normal bounds for 30m.
Recommended short-term workarounds for FastCart:
- Reduce client-side max_context_length where possible for the next 24 hours.
- If safe, avoid batching multiple long-context prompts in the same call.
Next steps:
- Product and SRE are evaluating an expedited patch vs. backport for INF-3421 (KV-cache eviction changes). We will provide an ETA within 48 hours.

Neha Kapoor
Senior Account Lead, Redwood Inference

Olivia — sending this now unless you ask for edits. Also sharing the SRE playbook excerpt and the steering policy for your ops team (attached).
